steps.name: Jori
steps.text: Good morning, Your Excellency.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Good morning again, Jori. Please, see to the others.

steps.name: Jori
steps.text: Yes, Father.

steps.name: Frightened Sarkaz
steps.text: Father Abbot, we...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Much has happened of late, Sural. I understand your unease.

steps.name: Frightened Sarkaz
steps.text: Should we have come? Would those people from Laterano...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: It'll be alright.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: All who dwell in the Sanctilaminium Ambrosii are welcome in this chapel. That's how things have been for the last ten years.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Sit up front, Sural. Just like always. No need to worry.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Laterans do not interrupt a communion in progress.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Please, take your seats.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Join me in a moment of prayer. Wait, listen, and feel the peace and tranquility.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I am Stefano Torregrossa, abbot of the Sanctilaminium Ambrosii.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: The words 'believer' and 'kin' are not used here.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: The mundane world has certain conceptions of the Sankta and the Sarkaz. Order and chaos. Peace and war. Angels and devils. We share the same conceptions.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Our halos and horns are our most distinctive features, symbols etched in the very essence of our life. Our existence alone draws the attention of others.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Yet we have seen the sun rise and set thousands of times together, and we gather here today to partake in communion, to share shelter and blessing.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: We have spent varying lengths of time here at the abbey, but even the newcomers amongst us have been here for more than a decade.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: For a much longer time, we had no way of knowing whether we had been abandoned or forgotten. We did not know what perils the path ahead would hold, that we would meet at a fork of which no one could know.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: We had conflicts. We had secrets. But we tried to accept one another.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: We know the names and habits of everyone in this chapel. We shared food and sheltered one another from wind and rain.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: We fought beasts and bandits together. We built houses and paved roads together. We plowed fields and harvested them together.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: We were brothers and sisters. We loved each other, and treasured one another's peace and happiness as our own.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: The bonds that tie us went beyond any physical trait or telepathic connection, transcended any differences in faith or ideology.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Yet, after having endured the long night, it was the fleeting cold before the dawn that overcame us.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: The nuncios from Laterano, the Executors, and... emissaries from a distant realm... they all had their own plans, brought new hope, and forced painful choices.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: We lost our battered pillars to fire, and our respected and trusted brothers to conflict...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Stefano Torregrossa sought that which was most good, even if the answer was an unproven one. For this, I seek your forgiveness.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Sanctilaminium Ambrosii is not Paradise. But it is our common home.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I have faith that we will make the same choice.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Now, I invite you to take communion.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Does it hurt?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Could be worse.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: You put on a brave face, but I can hear your teeth chattering.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: The barrel of a rifle will never be worse than a bullet.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You can have one of those, too, if you want.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I can feel your seething anger.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: You're angry that I violated the purity of your faith. That proves you're thinking as a Lateran.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Your mission is to bring the Sanctilaminium Ambrosii back to Laterano, and to help the lost Lateran kin there. My mission is to preserve what makes Laterano, Laterano.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Set your sentimentality aside, Lemuen. We're in agreement here.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Enough with your sophistry.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Did you learn it from the Victorian nobles, or Columbian merchants, Legatus Oren?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I said it, the sudden appearance of beasts will frighten wanderers. I'm not going to stand by and watch a massacre happen.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: The commandos will be in position any moment now. You can't stop me.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I can incapacitate you, then deal with them.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: You may have surprised me once, but it won't work again. Not unless you actually put a bullet in my brain.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Is that so?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Lemuen? Oren? Don't tell me you're really going to—
A loud crack interrupts the exchange.

Again, and then again, before anyone could react, so loud that it sounds like the patron firearm was being fired right next to their ears. They could not even hear their own heartbeats for a few seconds.
The projectile leaves a long trail in the damp morning air.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am Executor Federico of the Laterano Notarial Hall. That was a warning shot.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Cardinal Aide Lemuen, Legatus Oren, and Technician Serpilia of the Sixth Tribunal. I command you to cease your pointless altercation at once.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I see no need to understand your positions or mediate your conflict.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The mission remains incomplete. Newly emerged factors continue to present a risk of escalation. This monastery needs order.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If there is no contradiction between you, yet conflict remains unresolved; if empathy is not enough to prevent a community from disintegrating...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Then I will be order.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That warning shot was also intended for the special forces outside. Lateran troops will not enter the Sanctilaminium Ambrosii without my express authorization.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You were the one who deployed them, Oren. You will restrain them. Order them to pull back one kilometer and stand by.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Lemuen and Serpilia. The two of you have been in contact with the Sankta and Sarkaz populations here. You will reassure them and prevent the situation from escalating.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Meet me in the chapel once you have finished your task. Richele has uncovered a lead and is following it.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I will find the one responsible for this situation.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You will act now.
Now, I invite you to take communion.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Guess I didn't make it in time.
Richele peeks through a gap in the door and sees the gathered crowd return to their seats with sacramental bread and wine.
In the chancel, the aging abbot looks up toward the door, almost as though he is looking at Richele.
Richele thinks for a moment, then closes the door. He thinks for another moment, then takes out a spare gun grip, which he uses to latch the door handle.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Almost. All that's left is to wait for it to... finish.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Hm? Did Federico run into trouble? I guess I'm the only one taking care of things here now.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: What a chore.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I should have taken the mission to search for the missing Legatus in Sargon. It might have been a little far, but dealing with the people of the sand has got to be less complicated.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Am I doomed to be a workaholic? Truly, our fate lies not in our hands.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Let's see... patron firearm in good working order.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: If everyone inside... is one bullet per head enough? Don't tell me I'll have to use my fists...

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I should apply for paid leave once I get back to Laterano. The Notarial Hall had better approve it, considering my workload.
